claims.message: Pickle-like deserialization can execute attacker-controlled code.

labels.rationale: indico/core/emails.py:153-154 opens the supplied path and pickle.load deserializes its bytes before validation, substantiating a code-capable deserialization primitive. Lines 142-147 show the intended producer uses tempfile.mkstemp and pickle.dump for failed mail; lines 162-165 pass command paths into the resend helper. This file does not establish that an adversary can supply or replace the file consumed by an operator, nor that all callers enforce the intended trusted-file boundary. Without callers, file/directory ownership and permissions, and the operational path-selection contract, a HIGH repository defect cannot be confirmed or dismissed.
labels.repair: If an untrusted producer or writable recovery-file boundary exists, replace the pickle recovery format with a non-executable, schema-validated representation covering the actual email and attachment types, and reject untrusted legacy files. If files are intentionally trusted operator artifacts, enforce and document that boundary and verify ownership/permissions before loading; a blanket format substitution is not justified from this file alone.
missing_facts: Whether any caller or operator workflow can select attacker-supplied recovery files.
Who can create, replace, or modify recovery paths and their parent directories, including TEMP_DIR.
Whether recovery records are authenticated or constrained by callers beyond the supplied source.

evidence.observation: Secure temporary-file producer, unrestricted path argument at the local helper, and pickle.load sink; caller trust remains unproven.

labels.rationale: emails.py:153-154 really unpickles bytes from a caller-supplied path, so executable deserialization is present. The matching producer stores failed-email data with tempfile.mkstemp and pickle.dump at lines 142-147. The only discovered in-tree call to resend_failed_email is resend_failed_emails_cmd at lines 162-165, reached from the local Click recovery command at cli/core.py:101-115, where the operator supplies file paths. No remote input route, attacker-controlled pickle bytes, elevated execution relative to that operator, or adversarial write capability over recovery files is established. Ordinary email text serialized with pickle.dump is not itself a way to inject pickle opcodes. The dangerous primitive alone does not justify a HIGH security defect in this recovery workflow.
labels.repair: No mandatory security repair is justified by the supplied trust boundary. If recovery files must cross an untrusted boundary, replace pickle with a versioned, validated data-only representation and restrict recovery file ownership/path handling; that requirement is not established here.
missing_facts: A less-trusted actor's ability to choose or alter bytes that a more-privileged recovery operator will load.
Actual recovery directory ownership/permissions and any operational policy accepting externally supplied recovery files.

evidence.observation: Failed send task invokes internal recovery-file producer.
mkstemp producer, pickle.load consumer, and local wrapper.
Local command accepts operator-supplied existing file paths.
Default configured temporary directory; actual deployed permissions are not supplied.
